name: tier1_props_review
_comment: THE PROPS SCENE — the combined room, with orc work standing in it.
Geometry, player station, carve and legibility points are tier1_combined_review's, copied
verbatim and not to be edited independently: the props are judged ON THE LANDED SURFACES,
and a scene that drifted from the one the floors and walls were ratified in would be judging
THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION THIS SCENE EXISTS TO ANSWER, routed from the wall lane and quoted
in CC-SESSION-tier2-props.md: 'the props session PASSES only if orc work is visible AS
STANDING OBJECTS IN THE LIT RADIUS of the walked scene.' Every placement below is inside the
carried lamp's reach from the player's station, because a prop in the dark answers nothing.
It is also #167's exit: 'the prop/overlay pass gives wall tops world-placed OBJECTS standing
on them ... so §8.3.1 does not reach them.'
_station_trail: (5,13) — route peak. REJECTED: put the map edge in frame (see above).
_void_note: THE VOID IS NOT IN THIS FILE. Which cells are void is a wall-family question and it is set
per capture — see tools/tier1_floors/capture_combined.sh and the --void-ring it passes, and
the flag's own documentation on Tier1BoundaryWall.Apply for why that is a command-line
decision rather than a manifest edit.
_legibility: Wall faces are probed at the FLOOR cell they stand over, exactly as the wall gate scene
probed them: the probe reads a cell's delivered luminance, and a face is not a cell.
Nothing east of x=10 or south of y=20 is declared — at this camera it is outside the frame,
and a still cannot check ground it does not contain.

_carve_note: Row 15 is carved in two pieces either side of x=5, which leaves ONE CELL STANDING at (5,15).
That is the island: floor on all four sides and on all four diagonals, so it is the only
geometry in any review scene that puts four OUTER corners in frame. Inherited unchanged from
tier1_wall_review — every rect in this list is that spec's, byte for byte, so a comparison
between the two scenes is a comparison of stations and of nothing else.
_props_note: TWO PROPS LANDED, ONE DID NOT.
B-PROP-001 (9800) and B-PROP-003 (9820) are style-matched generations conditioned on the
LANDED FRAME and downsampled 2:1 to the family's native 32px. B-PROP-002, the barricade, is
ABSENT: six generations came back as fences or floor-fills and two composition passes read
as ladders. It is recorded as outstanding in tools/tier2_props/MANIFEST.json rather than
landed badly — an asset nobody can name is worse than a gap.
The fire's ENGINE LIGHT is not attached in this build. The prop is judged as an object
first, which is what the identity card's carried-only capture is for; the two-source scene

props.why: B-PROP-001, the boundary marker stone. One tile SW of the station and unambiguously inside the lit pool — the routed acceptance criterion is orc work visible AS A STANDING OBJECT IN THE LIT RADIUS, so the first prop is placed where that question cannot be dodged.

B-PROP-003, the orc fire. Three tiles east of the station: far enough that it is not read as part of the player's own pool, close enough to be legible. Its engine light is NOT yet attached — this build judges the object, and the two-source scene is the next round.

B-PROP-001 again, at 5 tiles — the same object at the far end of the lit radius. Two placements of one prop is the cheapest test of §8.3.1 available before the variant family exists: if it reads as a motif at two, it will at four.
